evidence: forwardHumanMessage gateway forwards only source/destination/request/privacy arguments; ProductionSessionWorkers::authorize_forward_source checks participant, settled-message and protected-content policy before capture.
snapshot_forward_attachments caps count at six and each opened regular file at 32 MiB; size is exact/nonzero and checked against declared source size when present.

Source owner db_path canonical parent supplies the trusted root. Derived account/issuer/request length-delimited SHA-256 scope and ordered index/digest names do not use caller-supplied destination directories.
Unix file open uses O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK; Windows uses FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT. Opened handle metadata must remain regular; bounded reads reject changed length.

create_new private temporary file is flushed and sync_all'ed, closed, then atomically hard_link-published without overwriting. New and identical-orphan reuse both synchronize the directory on Unix. Temporary guard owns only the unique file it created.

HumanForwardBatch is stored with the existing expected-value metadata CAS only after complete capture. Interrupted or failed capture can leave unreferenced complete files but cannot initiate a destination POST.
append_human_message_with_context now verifies the complete attachment set into at most six successful 32 MiB payload buffers before the first resource POST for that target.
read_forward_attachment_bytes validates pin version, exact nonzero bounded size, lowercase SHA-256, account/issuer/request/index path identity, regular handle and actual digest.
Verified Vec buffers are moved through into_iter directly into upload_direct_message_resource_bytes_for_user and multipart Part::bytes; the upload path does not reopen the pinned path.

The ordinary send gateway calls public append_human_message with no forward context. Its normalization discards caller-provided forwardSnapshot. Forward capture overwrites any source attachment's old forwardSnapshot with freshly admitted evidence.

Credential-bound uploader checks expected Human account and configured issuer origin, then rechecks credentials after response headers and after body completion. No bearer/session value enters snapshot metadata.

Source authorization is rechecked for every remaining destination. Missing/corrupt pin errors are per-target results persisted in the source batch and pending transcript. Ordinary sync continues to history because delivery returns the failed-target batch normally.

v1 forwarding pending rows are excluded from generic destination outbox replay; they recover through the source-owned complete batch. Existing persisted resource IDs may settle an ambiguous send without re-uploading.
HumanForwardBatch version, decoder, validation and metadata CAS semantics remain unchanged. Legacy attachment JSON is not normalized into fabricated pins on load.
Missing forwardSnapshot fails only in the delivery reader; unfinished targets retain visible errors and original immutable legacy intent. Completed targets are skipped and preserved.
Text-only version-one recovery bypasses the attachment reader and retains the existing flow. Exact bytes can repair a new pin; no fallback reads the mutable original source path.
Neither capture nor retry deletes source/cache/user files, prior journal records or retained snapshot files. Existing destination pending and completed rows retain their owners.
Binary multipart fixture parses actual request payload bytes; it does not use lossy UTF-8 as the byte oracle.
First upload observes independent SQLite whole-batch metadata and all snapshot files before acknowledging that upload.
Actual child process is killed in an in-flight accepted first message POST; reopen/replay settles its stable nonce and submits the previously unsubmitted target.
Cache replacement/deletion tests compare both destinations' actual multipart bytes and persisted target resources to independent original fixture bytes.

Two-attachment missing/corrupt/oversized/directory cases damage the second pin while the first remains valid; explicit retry and ordinary sync must add no resource/message POST and must continue history.

Six-attachment privacy case mutates the second pin after the first upload, confirms the disk is still mutated during the second upload, and requires its actual multipart bytes to remain original. This directly exercises the validated-buffer lifetime.

Focused owner tests cover exact 32 MiB boundary, count/size/regular-input admission, safe non-overwrite publication and temporary cleanup, scoped paths/aliases/symlinks, immutable source loss/reopen, and legacy journal preservation.

integrationAssessment.subject: Strict source-journal recovery scanner
evidence: resume_human_forward_batches scans the existing native conversation directory, checks entries and existing database paths, and opens the same SandAgentDb Human owner rather than consuming the visible roster projection.
IO, owner-open and journal-decode errors propagate. Existing request identity and account/issuer filtering are preserved. Completed batches are skipped without mutation.

Each unfinished destination still passes authorize_forward_source and current account/issuer validation. Policy denial remains durable per-target failure and returns the batch normally, allowing independent history; storage/decoding failure remains an error.
The scan does not create a second owner, recreate missing conversation databases, delete user state or send data merely because a directory was discovered.
integrationAssessment.limitation: This does not establish multi-AppHost cross-source request uniqueness or all-or-none recovery across every source. Missing physical source storage cannot be reconstructed by this scanner.

integrationAssessment.subject: Same-batch completed progress cannot regress
evidence: store_forward_batch first validates the incoming batch and checks immutable source, text, attachment, context and ordered destination/nonce identities.

Before replacing an existing batch it rejects any prior.completed && !requested.completed pair, so reading fresh metadata immediately before CAS cannot admit a stale caller snapshot that reopens an already completed destination.

The existing set_metadata_if_unchanged still compares the observed journal key and CASes the full SQLite metadata record; another writer between observation and write is rejected without erasing its record.

The retained independent-handle stale-progress test requires a stale error, unchanged settled state and fresh-load continuation/reopen. The retained concurrent test uses a barrier and independent SQLite handles, requiring exactly one durable winner plus retained unrelated metadata.
integrationAssessment.limitation: Static review of the actual tests and code is not proof that concurrent execution passed; containing-H Actions remains required.

integrationAssessment.subject: Metadata type corruption remains a storage error
evidence: read_forward_journal_value now reads metadata and explicitly requires a JSON object before extracting humanForwardBatches; both load and store call this narrow helper.
The generic SandAgentDb::get_metadata behavior and its other callers were not modified.
Valid object with absent journal remains absence; malformed hex/JSON and valid non-object JSON cannot be silently converted to an empty journal when an owner is cached.

The existing Human corruption test now crosses cold/cached owner modes with independent invalid hex, invalid JSON, null, array and string byte fixtures, preserving the actual killed process, zero new send/history, unchanged damaged bytes and exact-repair recovery assertions.

integrationAssessment.subject: NMR-48 attachment behavior remains composed through the existing owners
evidence: New strict journal reads and monotonic completion do not rewrite attachment pins, legacy attachment JSON, source snapshots or completed destination resources.

The existing batch load still feeds destination append through source authorization. Legacy unpinned and missing/corrupt pin failures remain target results rather than metadata decode failures, so their ordinary-history continuation behavior remains distinct from a corrupt journal.

All target snapshot buffers remain verified before any new resource POST and are moved into the existing credential-bound bytes uploader; the retained two-attachment negative and six-attachment mid-upload mutation tests directly constrain that behavior.
The original generic v1 forwarding outbox exclusion and source-owned recovery design remain intact.

findings.rootCause: With an already cached source owner, SandAgentDb::get_metadata mapped a valid JSON non-object metadata value to None; load_forward_batches treated that as an absent journal and strict recovery could silently skip it.

findings.resolution: Narrow read_forward_journal_value requires metadata to be a JSON object for both journal load and store; generic metadata APIs remain unchanged.
